segments: page 358. The Aleppines, the citizens of the town, [sided with] the Yaruqis who were outside Aleppo.
And the Yaruqis sent to 'Imad al-Din Zengi, the lord of Sinjar,
and brought him to them
so that they might hand Aleppo over to him.
The Aleppines, however, sent and threatened him,
that if he did not leave and go away,
they would bind him maliciously.
And when he departed and went away,
'Izz al-Din Mas'ud came to Aleppo,
went up to its citadel, and took control.
And he took the mother of al-Malik al-Salih as his wife,
and sent her to Mosul.
And he opened the storehouses in which boundless treasures had been laid up since the days of Nur al-Din and of Zengi his father,
and he sent them all to Mosul.
And he made peace with Bohemond the Prince, the lord of Antioch, for a period of two years.
And he left in the citadel of Aleppo Nur al-Din, his young son,
and appointed a governor for him.
And he himself went and encamped in the meadow of Qara Hisar,
and sent an envoy to his brother 'Imad al-Din Zengi, the lord of Sinjar,
because he had set out with all his household, his sons, and his retainers,
and had come to Qarqisya
in order to go and take refuge with Saladin,
so that he might help him and restore to him the kingdom of his father.
Then 'Imad al-Din replied to his brother's envoy:
"I will not return at all,
unless he gives me Aleppo, or Mosul, or the whole of Mesopotamia."
Then 'Izz al-Din agreed to give him Aleppo—
the city alone—
while his own son would remain in the citadel.
And 'Imad al-Din replied:
"I do not agree to be a governor under your son in Aleppo."
And 'Izz al-Din answered [saying]:
"I will add for you 'Arban, and Majdal, and other villages along the Khabur."
And when 'Imad al-Din contended and would not accept,
the nobles advised:
"Give him Aleppo and its citadel,
and do not quarrel with your brother over something that you cannot protect—
nor can he—
from Saladin.
And what, pray, have you left in it that you should spare it? For lo, you have carried away all its wealth to Mosul!"
So both brothers swore an oath to one another,
and 'Imad al-Din took Aleppo and its territory,
and he left Sinjar to 'Izz al-Din, along with Mosul.
And in this year, a large ship of the Franks sailed to Damietta,
because they had peace with the Muslims.
